### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. cardiospondylocarpofacial syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.496)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-168638, Reactome:R-HSA-202424, Reactome:R-HSA-450302, Reactome:R-HSA-450321, Reactome:R-HSA-5357956)

**Proposed mechanism:** TAB2 (HGNC:11019) —BINDS→ NF-kappa B signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-69760); MAP3K7 (HGNC:18070) —BINDS→ NF-kappa B signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-69760); NF-kappa B signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-69760) —LEADS_TO→ Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia (HP:0008419); NF-kappa B signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-69760) —LEADS_TO→ Facial dysmorphism (HP:0001999); NF-kappa B signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-69760) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital heart disease (HP:0001627). Haploinsufficiency of either TAB2 or MAP3K7 leads to a dysfunctional NF-kappa B signaling pathway, which in turn causes the overlapping phenotypes of spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, facial dysmorphism, and congenital heart disease seen in both MONDO:0014000 and cardiospondylocarpofacial syndrome (MONDO:0008005).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in TAB2 or MAP3K7 with loss-of-function effects in one disease and gain-of-function effects in the other would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if MONDO:0014000 and cardiospondylocarpofacial syndrome were found to be caused by entirely separate signaling pathways that do not converge on NF-kappa B, this would also falsify the hypothesis. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of the NF-kappa B signaling pathway in these conditions could lead to the development of targeted therapies that modulate this pathway for the benefit of patients with either MONDO:0014000 or cardiospondylocarpofacial syndrome.

#### 2. frontometaphyseal dysplasia 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.474)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-168638, Reactome:R-HSA-202424, Reactome:R-HSA-450302, Reactome:R-HSA-450321, Reactome:R-HSA-5357956)

**Proposed mechanism:** TAB2 (HGNC:11472) —BINDS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP468); MAP3K7 (HGNC:6850) —BINDS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP468); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP468) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0002711); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP468) —LEADS_TO→ Craniosynostosis (HP:0005409). Haploinsufficiency of TAB2 and MAP3K7 leads to dysregulation of the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, which in turn contributes to the skeletal dysplasia and craniosynostosis observed in these diseases.

**How to falsify it:** If variants in TAB2 or MAP3K7 with predicted loss-of-function or haploinsufficiency effects are found at a high frequency (>1%) in the gnomAD database in populations not known to have these diseases, it would challenge the causal link. _(variant: gnomAD v2.1.1 exome data for variants in TAB2 and MAP3K7)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of TAB2 and MAP3K7 in the NF-kappaB pathway could lead to the identification of common therapeutic targets for both MONDO:0014000 and frontometaphyseal dysplasia 2, potentially involving modulation of inflammatory or bone remodeling processes.

#### 3. incontinentia pigmenti  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.473)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-168638, Reactome:R-HSA-202424, Reactome:R-HSA-450302, Reactome:R-HSA-450321, Reactome:R-HSA-5357956)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in IKBKG —DISRUPTS→ IKBKG (HGNC:5441); IKBKG (HGNC:5441) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP517); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP517) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal skin development (HP:0000953); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP517) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal hair development (HP:0001045). Pathogenic variants in IKBKG lead to loss-of-function, disrupting the NF-kappaB signaling pathway. This disruption impairs downstream gene expression critical for normal skin and hair development, manifesting as the phenotypes observed in incontinentia pigmenti and potentially contributing to developmental abnormalities in the other disease.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of pathogenic variants in IKBKG in individuals with either disease, or demonstration that IKBKG mutations do not impact the NF-kappaB signaling pathway in these contexts. _(variant: None)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the NF-kappaB signaling pathway could offer therapeutic avenues for both conditions, provided the specific downstream consequences can be modulated without exacerbating other disease features.

#### 4. Blau syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.458)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-168638, Reactome:R-HSA-450302, Reactome:R-HSA-450321)

**Proposed mechanism:** NOD2 (HGNC:19874) —DISRUPTS→ NOD2 signaling pathway (WP:WP4035); TAB2 (HGNC:23773) —DISRUPTS→ NOD2 signaling pathway (WP:WP4035); NOD2 signaling pathway (WP:WP4035) —INCREASES→ Granulomatous inflammation (HP:0030155); NOD2 signaling pathway (WP:WP4035) —INCREASES→ Polyarthritis (HP:0002835); NOD2 signaling pathway (WP:WP4035) —INCREASES→ Uveitis (HP:0000543); NOD2 signaling pathway (WP:WP4035) —INCREASES→ Skin rash (HP:0001061). Gain-of-function mutations in NOD2 (Blau syndrome) and potentially other genetic factors affecting the NOD2 signaling pathway (EOS) lead to increased granulomatous inflammation, polyarthritis, uveitis, and skin rash.

**How to falsify it:** If common variants in NOD2 or TAB2 with frequencies >1% in gnomAD are found to be strongly associated with Early-onset Sarcoidosis, it would suggest the proposed mechanistic link is less specific or that other pathways are primarily involved. _(variant: rs2066844)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the NOD2 signaling pathway or its downstream effectors could offer therapeutic strategies for both Blau syndrome and Early-onset Sarcoidosis, potentially through anti-inflammatory agents or modulators of cytokine production.

#### 5. immunodeficiency 15a  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.423)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-168638, Reactome:R-HSA-202424, Reactome:R-HSA-5357956)

**Proposed mechanism:** TAB2 (HGNC:11491) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP400); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP400) —LEADS_TO→ Immune dysregulation (HP:0002715); IKBKB (HGNC:5464) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP400); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP400) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002705). Loss-of-function mutations in TAB2 cause Omenn syndrome (MONDO:0014000) by disrupting the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, leading to immune dysregulation. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in IKBKB cause immunodeficiency 15a (MONDO:0032599) by disrupting the same NF-kappaB signaling pathway, resulting in immunodeficiency.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that TAB2 and IKBKB mutations do not converge on the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, or that variants in these genes are common in the general population (e.g., gnomAD allele frequency > 1% for pathogenic variants).

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of the NF-kappaB pathway in these distinct immunodeficiencies could reveal common therapeutic targets for modulating immune responses and improving treatment strategies for patients with these rare conditions.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with pathogenic variants in TAB2 or IKBKB who exhibit phenotypes entirely unrelated to either Pfeiffer syndrome or severe combined immunodeficiency, and who do not show any signs of NF-kappaB pathway dysregulation. _(variant: N/A)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the NF-kappaB signaling pathway could offer therapeutic avenues for both diseases, potentially through modulation of upstream regulators or downstream effectors, although the specific therapeutic strategies would need to be tailored to the distinct clinical presentations.
